summary: Round 6 verify. All five round-5 items measured killed in a review tree at the staged bytes, plus seven earlier open findings re-measured killed. (1) SegmentCommit.Attribution blank check deleted -> only AttributedDeltaTest#aBlankPodIdOnTheWireIsREFUSED fails. (2) CheckpointWriter pointerEpoch = 1L -> only CheckpointWriterContentTest#theSlotPointsAtTheDeltaThatAppliedNotTheOneAfterIt fails, on the literal 4L. (3) v0 single-segment encode branch deleted -> AttributedDeltaTest#aDeltaWithNoAttributionEncodesExactlyAsBefore fails on bytes[7] (it passed on bytes[4]). (4) writeAttribution IllegalStateException -> return -> only aDeltaMixingAttributedAndUnattributedSegmentsIsREFUSED fails. (5) comment/.as() corrections verified true: grep of every src/main outside format finds only CommitLog:335 and CheckpointWriter:150, both on the WRITE path, so 'nothing in src/main reads it back' holds. Re-measured killed: LocalSequencer observe(requests, 0L) -> LocalSequencerCheckpointTest; pre-ADR merge lambda -> aRestartedPodsSecondCommitIsNotRefusedByTheDeadIncarnationsWatermark; version > VERSION_ATTRIBUTED -> anUNKNOWNVersionSTOPSRatherThanGuessingTheLayout; PodState's three invariants deleted -> three PodStateInvariantTest cases; CommitRequest incarnation validation deleted -> CommitRequestTest#aBlankOrNullIncarnationIsRefused; attributionLen len<0 dropped -> bothAttributionLengthsAreBoundedInBothDirections; count<=0 weakened to count==0 -> both count tests; attribution hoisted to once per delta -> everySegmentKeepsItsOwnTripleAcrossABatch + both attributed goldens; DefaultIngest minting per flush -> IngestCommitPathTest#theIncarnationIsMintedOncePerIngestInstanceAndDiffersBetweenTwoOfThem; CommitLog flushSeq constant -> both CommitLogAttributionTest cases; Checkpoint always VERSION_ATTRIBUTED -> 13 tests including GoldenCheckpointTest byte-identity. RED RECORDS: the nine re-recorded reds were minted by removing the guard, running the test, observing failure and restoring. That is an honest red. tdd-red.sh records only ids the JUnit XML reports as FAILED, so a passing test cannot mint one, and testing.md rule 3 states outright that the gate raises the cost of skipping rather than proving virtue. For a test that pins a guard a reviewer named in a later round, guard-removal is the only red available and it is stronger evidence than an ordinary one: it is a mutation kill, which is what rule 9 asks for. I reproduced all nine kills independently. No assertion was weakened in this round: the only changes to existing assertions are .as() message text, and CheckpointWriterContentTest gained an assertion rather than losing one. Tree restored clean after every mutation (git diff --quiet); :format:test :sequencer:test :ingest:test green at the staged bytes.
